source.author: Gareth A. Jones
source.title: Primitive permutation groups containing a cycle
source.statement: Theorem 1.2 k=1: if G is a finite primitive permutation group of degree n, does not contain A_n and contains a cycle with one fixed point, then (a) AGL_d(q)<=G<=AΓL_d(q), n=q^d, d>=1 and q a prime power; or (b) G=L_2(p) or PGL_2(p), n=p+1 with p>=5 prime; or (c) G=M_11, M_12 or M_24 in degree 12,12 or 24 respectively.
source.scope: The exact public statement was read from v1; the paper says its proof relies heavily on the classification of finite simple groups. Its proof was not replayed, independently reviewed or formally checked.
